summary: Albert Fish, an elderly house painter in New York, abducted and murdered children in the 1920s, including Grace Budd, whom he cannibalized; a taunting letter led to his 1934 arrest and 1936 execution.

evidence.note: first abduction covered: boy taken on Staten Island in 1924
mobs attack suspected kidnappers after the Gaffney abduction
national kidnapping wave of 1932-33 and the Lindbergh case tied to Fish's crimes
crank letters and sensational press coverage targeting grieving families
detective planted false leads in a gossip column to keep the case alive
stationery traced to a rooming house leads police to arrest Fish
guest recounts learning of her descent from Fish's brother
Westchester records office where the original letter was taken
childhood in an orphanage after his father's death, briefly covered
self-harm with needles and burning described at length
executed in the electric chair in January 1936

notes: Transcript renders the 1924 victim as Francis McDonald; standard spelling McDonnell used. Lifespan 1870-1936 and US origin (Washington, DC) from general knowledge. Not partial_life: the story centres on his crimes but sketches his whole life. Joe Coleman documentary and guest's family history treated as legacy (reaches_present). Mental illness gets real time but has no theme.
